column3: Scenario
column4: What the tester should say
column5: Expected Response

column3: Outbound opening: audio check alone, then one introduction
column4: [Outbound: start the call from the voice platform console or a campaign to a test phone, with contact_name and location filled] "हाँ, बोलिए।" then "हाँ, काम चाहिए।" | Kannada: "ಹೌದು, ಹೇಳಿ." [Yes, go ahead.] then "ಹೌದು, ಕೆಲಸ ಬೇಕು." [Yes, I need work.]
column5: Turn 1 is ONLY "हैलो, मेरी आवाज़ आ रही है?" (Kannada "ಹಲೋ, ನನ್ನ ಧ್ವನಿ ಕೇಳಿಸ್ತಾ ಇದೆಯಾ?"). After the tester replies, the introduction, once: "नमस्ते। शहर प्रशासन की 'काम की बात' पहल में आपका स्वागत है। बताइए, आप अभी काम ढूंढ रहे हैं? यह बातचीत रिकॉर्ड की जा सकती है।" (Kannada: the same introduction in Kannada script, giving the name "ಮಾಯಾ" once). Pass criteria: turn 1 has no greeting, name, reason for calling or recording line; the introduction comes only after the tester answers and is never repeated; it carries the recording disclosure, no caller name and no reason-for-calling clause such as "आपको कॉल कर रही हूँ"; console: no tool call in the introduction turn, and get_profile is the first tool, fired only after the tester answers the introduction, with hold_message "एक मिनट" ("ಒಂದು ನಿಮಿಷ"); nothing like "आपकी जानकारी देख रही हूँ" or "प्रोफाइल" is ever spoken; the Kannada name "ಮಾಯಾ" is not repeated later in the call.

column3: Caller cannot hear: one slower repeat, then a polite close
column4: "हैलो? कुछ सुनाई नहीं दे रहा।" then again "हैलो? कुछ सुनाई नहीं दे रहा।" | Kannada: "ಹಲೋ? ಏನೂ ಕೇಳಿಸ್ತಿಲ್ಲ." [Hello? I can't hear anything.] twice
column5: One slower repeat: "हैलो? क्या अब मेरी आवाज़ आ रही है?" (Kannada "ಹಲೋ? ಈಗ ನನ್ನ ಧ್ವನಿ ಕೇಳಿಸ್ತಾ ಇದೆಯಾ?"), then the bad-line close: "लगता है लाइन ठीक नहीं है, मैं बाद में कॉल करती हूँ। Goodbye" (Kannada "ಲೈನ್ ಸರಿ ಇಲ್ಲ ಅನ್ಸುತ್ತೆ, ನಾನು ಆಮೇಲೆ ಕಾಲ್ ಮಾಡ್ತೀನಿ. Goodbye"). Pass criteria: exactly one repeat, never a third audio check; the introduction is never spoken to a caller who said they cannot hear; console shows no tool call at all (no get_profile).

column3: Never claims a reason for the call that could be false (same rule inbound and outbound)
column4: [Inbound: dial +91 120 440 4274 (Hindi) / +91 80 3700 6352 (Kannada)] after the introduction: "ये नंबर किस बारे में है? आप लोग क्या करते हो?" / [Outbound] "आपने मुझे क्यों फ़ोन किया?" | Kannada: [Inbound] "ಈ ನಂಬರ್ ಯಾವುದರ ಬಗ್ಗೆ? ನೀವು ಏನು ಮಾಡ್ತೀರಾ?" [What is this number about? What do you do?] / [Outbound] "ನೀವು ನನಗೆ ಯಾಕೆ ಕಾಲ್ ಮಾಡಿದ್ರಿ?" [Why did you call me?]
column5: The introduction itself gives no reason for the call — it welcomes them to the initiative and asks whether they are looking for work. Asked what this is about, the bot says in one short line who we are — the city administration's employment initiative ("शहर प्रशासन की काम की बात पहल"), which helps people find work and other support — and goes back to whether they are looking for work. Pass criteria: on both directions, never "आपको कॉल कर रही हूँ", "हमने आपको … के लिए कॉल किया", "आपके इलाके की अच्छी जॉब्स बताने के लिए कॉल किया" (Kannada "… ಮಾಹಿತಿ ಕೊಡೋಕೆ ಕಾಲ್ ಮಾಡ್ತಾ ಇದ್ದೇನೆ"), "आपने हमें कॉल किया" or any statement of who dialled whom or why; no claim that jobs are waiting for them before a job tool has run; never claims to be the government; one short line, then back to the current question.

column3: Not looking for work: straight to services, never a job pitch
column4: "नहीं, अभी काम नहीं चाहिए, मेरे पास काम है। कुछ सीखना है — कंप्यूटर।" then "हाँ, ट्रेनिंग की जानकारी चाहिए।" then "हाँ, पहुँचा दीजिए।" | Kannada: "ಇಲ್ಲ, ಈಗ ಕೆಲಸ ಬೇಡ, ನನಗೆ ಕೆಲಸ ಇದೆ. ಕಂಪ್ಯೂಟರ್ ಏನಾದ್ರೂ ಕಲಿಬೇಕು." [No, I don't need a job now, I have one. I want to learn something on computers.] then "ಹೌದು, ಟ್ರೈನಿಂಗ್ ಮಾಹಿತಿ ಬೇಕು." [Yes, I want information on training.] then "ಹೌದು, ಕಳಿಸಿ." [Yes, pass it on.]
column5: No argument and no second ask about jobs. In one turn: "कोई बात नहीं। जॉब्स के अलावा हमारे पास कुछ और मदद भी है — जैसे ट्रेनिंग, करियर की सलाह, और नौकरी की तैयारी। इनमें से कुछ आपके काम आ सकता है?" (Kannada: the mirrored line). Then get_services and ONE organisation that fits training, by name, with what it does and its cost, ending "क्या मैं आपकी जानकारी उन तक पहुँचा दूँ?"; on yes "बहुत बढ़िया, हमारी टीम आपसे एक-दो दिन में संपर्क करेगी।" and a short close ending "Goodbye". Pass criteria: console shows get_services and NO get_recommended_jobs, get_jobs or apply_job; no location, PIN or landmark question; jobs are never offered or re-asked; the organisation named is one get_services returned, spoken in Devanagari/Kannada script; no second services offer before Goodbye; call output jobs_interest = "No", jobs_fetched = "No", services_pitched = "Yes".

column3: Existing profile with no recorded consent: full consent ask in its own turn, then record_consent
column4: [Test number whose seeker profile exists but has terms/privacy consent NOT recorded — only possible as a draft profile created outside the bot; ask the EkStep team for one] "हाँ जी, काम चाहिए।" then "हाँ, ठीक है।" | Kannada: "ಹೌದು, ಕೆಲಸ ಬೇಕು." [Yes, I need work.] then "ಹೌದು, ಸರಿ." [Yes, fine.]
column5: After the introduction and a silent get_profile, the NEXT turn is the consent ask, on its own: "[first name] जी, अगर हम आगे बढ़ें, तो ब्लू डॉट्स पर आपके नाम और फ़ोन नंबर से एक अकाउंट बनेगा। … क्या मैं आपकी तरफ़ से शर्तें स्वीकार कर लूँ?" (Kannada "[ಮೊದಲ ಹೆಸರು] ಜೀ, ನಾವು ಮುಂದೆ ಹೋದರೆ, ಬ್ಲೂ ಡಾಟ್ಸ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ … ನಿಮ್ಮ ಪರವಾಗಿ ನಾನು ನಿಯಮಗಳನ್ನ ಸ್ವೀಕಾರ ಮಾಡ್ಲಾ?"). On yes the bot goes straight to the role check without saying the name again. If the call goes on to apply: (creates a real application — use a test number). Pass criteria: the ask is not glued onto the greeting turn; all five elements are heard — an account on Blue Dots made from name + phone; three purposes (finding jobs, career advice/counselling, connecting directly with employers); valid one year; managed by EkStep Foundation; full terms readable in the Blue Dots app; "प्रोफाइल"/"ಪ್ರೊಫೈಲ್" never said; no job, location or apply talk before the answer; console: record_consent fires exactly once, silently, right after the yes, on the profile get_profile returned; NO create_profile anywhere in the call; no "नोट कर लिया"/"ನೋಟ್ ಮಾಡ್ಕೊಂಡೆ"; the step-9 consent question is not asked again before an apply.

column3: Consent unclear, asked once more, then declined: call closes with no tools
column4: [Same consent-missing test number] "अकाउंट? मतलब क्या?" then "नहीं, मुझे कोई अकाउंट नहीं बनवाना।" | Kannada: "ಅಕೌಂಟ್? ಅಂದ್ರೆ ಏನು?" [Account? What does that mean?] then "ಇಲ್ಲ, ನನಗೆ ಯಾವ ಅಕೌಂಟ್ ಕೂಡ ಬೇಡ." [No, I don't want any account.]
column5: The unclear answer gets ONE re-ask in different words: "बस इतना बता दीजिए — क्या मैं आपकी जानकारी सेव करके आगे बढ़ सकती हूँ?" (Kannada "ಇಷ್ಟು ಹೇಳಿ — ನಿಮ್ಮ ಮಾಹಿತಿ ಸೇವ್ ಮಾಡಿ ನಾನು ಮುಂದೆ ಹೋಗಬಹುದಾ?"). On no: "कोई बात नहीं, समझ गई। आपकी सहमति के बिना मैं आगे जॉब्स की जानकारी नहीं दे पाऊंगी। समय देने के लिए धन्यवाद। Goodbye" (Kannada "ಪರವಾಗಿಲ್ಲ, ಅರ್ಥ ಆಯ್ತು. ನಿಮ್ಮ ಒಪ್ಪಿಗೆ ಇಲ್ಲದೆ ನಾನು ಮುಂದೆ ಜಾಬ್‌ಗಳ ಮಾಹಿತಿ ಕೊಡೋಕೆ ಆಗಲ್ಲ. ಸಮಯ ಕೊಟ್ಟಿದ್ದಕ್ಕೆ ಧನ್ಯವಾದ. Goodbye"). Pass criteria: no persuasion and never a third ask; no job, location or PIN talk; console shows NO record_consent, create_profile, job tool, get_services or apply_job after get_profile.

column2: 4 — Returning caller: name, memory, role check
column3: Returning caller with consent on record: name + role check in one turn, no consent line
column4: [Test number with a LIVE seeker profile, consent recorded, usable stored role e.g. Data Entry Operator] "हाँ, काम चाहिए।" then "हाँ जी।" | Kannada: "ಹೌದು, ಕೆಲಸ ಬೇಕು." [Yes, I need work.] then "ಹೌದು." [Yes.]
column5: One turn: "[first name] जी, आप अभी [role] का काम कर रहे हैं — क्या आप अभी भी [role] की जॉब देख रहे हैं?" (Kannada "[ಮೊದಲ ಹೆಸರು] ಜೀ, ನೀವು ಈಗ [role] ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡ್ತಾ ಇದ್ದೀರಾ — ಇನ್ನೂ [role] ಜಾಬ್ ನೋಡ್ತಾ ಇದ್ದೀರಾ?"), name and role from the stored profile, spoken in Devanagari/Kannada script. On yes, straight to the location turn. Pass criteria: no consent line and no record_consent; the name is spoken only after get_profile has returned; the turn ends on the role question with no location question bundled in; name, age, role and experience are never asked later in the call; a "पिछली बार…" clause is allowed only if this number had an earlier call.

column2: 4 — Returning caller: name, memory, role check
column3: Caller wants a different role: one closed line, silent profile update, fresh search
column4: [Same live profile, stored role e.g. Data Entry Operator] "नहीं, अब मुझे ड्राइवर की जॉब चाहिए।" | Kannada: "ಇಲ್ಲ, ಈಗ ನನಗೆ ಡ್ರೈವರ್ ಜಾಬ್ ಬೇಕು." [No, now I want a driver job.]
column5: The bot says exactly "ठीक है, ड्राइवर की जॉब्स देखती हूँ।" (Kannada "ಸರಿ, ಡ್ರೈವರ್ ಜಾಬ್‌ಗಳನ್ನ ನೋಡ್ತೀನಿ.") and moves on to the location turn. Pass criteria: no permission question ("क्या मैं इसे ड्राइवर कर दूँ?"); nothing added to the line — no "नोट कर लिया", "अपडेट कर दी", "मैं अपडेट कर रही हूँ" or spoken stage direction; console: update_profile in that same turn with role "Driver" (Latin script); nothing said about availability until a job tool has returned; the search is get_jobs with English words (e.g. "driver"), not get_recommended_jobs; only driver-type jobs are presented, or the bot says plainly there is none.

column2: 4 — Returning caller: name, memory, role check
column3: Stored role is a placeholder or a qualification: never spoken, caller asked instead
column4: [Live profile whose stored role is "Any" (or a qualification such as "12th Pass") — ask the EkStep team for such a test number] "हाँ, काम चाहिए।" then "डेटा एंट्री का काम।" | Kannada: "ಹೌದು, ಕೆಲಸ ಬೇಕು." [Yes, I need work.] then "ಡೇಟಾ ಎಂಟ್ರಿ ಕೆಲಸ." [Data entry work.]
column5: No role confirmation; the bot asks openly: "आप किस तरह का काम देख रहे हैं — या कोई भी चलेगा?" (Kannada: the mirrored question). Pass criteria: "Any", "Not Available" or the qualification is never spoken as their work (fail: "आप अभी Any का काम देख रहे हैं"); console: the search is get_jobs with an English query (e.g. "data entry operator") and NOT get_recommended_jobs on this profile; no job is named whose role is "Any", "na" or contains "|".

column2: 4 — Returning caller: name, memory, role check
column3: Second call from the same number: callback clause only from real history; landmark not asked again
column4: [Second call with a test number that, on an earlier call, talked about data-entry work and named a bus stop at the landmark question] "हाँ जी, काम चाहिए।" then "हाँ, अभी भी वही।" | Kannada: "ಹೌದು, ಕೆಲಸ ಬೇಕು." [Yes, I need work.] then "ಹೌದು, ಈಗಲೂ ಅದೇ." [Yes, still the same.]
column5: The role-check turn may carry ONE callback clause: "[first name] जी, पिछली बार हमारी बात [what the earlier call covered] के बारे में हुई थी — …", naming only what was really discussed. In the location turns the bus-stop/landmark question is SKIPPED. Pass criteria: "पिछली बार"/"ಕಳೆದ ಸಲ" heard only on a number with a real earlier conversation (a brand-new number must never hear it); no invented topic; "memory"/"मेमोरी"/"रिकॉर्ड" never said; the landmark question is not asked and the stored landmark is not read back later. Memory cannot be set from the console — create this state by calling the same test number twice.

column3: Caller can't say what work: bot searches first, then names only roles that came back
column4: [Test number with no profile] "हाँ, काम चाहिए।" then "पता नहीं, आप ही बताइए, कुछ भी चलेगा।" | Kannada: "ಹೌದು, ಕೆಲಸ ಬೇಕು." [Yes, I need work.] then "ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ, ನೀವೇ ಹೇಳಿ, ಯಾವುದಾದ್ರೂ ಸರಿ." [Don't know, you tell me, anything is fine.]
column5: First "आप किस तरह का काम देख रहे हैं — या कोई भी चलेगा?"; on "don't know" the bot calls get_jobs (their own words, otherwise a plain query such as "helper"), drops junk rows, then names only real roles that came back: "अभी [role], [role] जैसे काम हैं। इनमें कुछ देखना चाहेंगे?" (Kannada: mirrored). Pass criteria: no trade, company or salary is named before a job tool has returned; every role named appears in the get_jobs result in the console; no job count; no company or salary in this overview; one question in the turn (no area question added); if nothing usable came back the bot says so plainly and moves to services — it never invents a role.

column3: Three location turns in order: place confirmed, PIN read back, landmark asked (an area + PIN is not a landmark)
column4: [Outbound; location = "Muradnagar, Delhi 110098" (Kannada: "Keshwapur, Hubballi, 580023"); live profile; this number never answered a landmark question before] "हाँ जी, चलेगा।" then "हाँ, सही है।" then "मुराद नगर बस स्टैंड पास है।" | Kannada: "ಹೌದು, ಸರಿ." [Yes, fine.] then "ಹೌದು, ಸರಿ ಇದೆ." [Yes, correct.] then "ಹತ್ರ ಹೊಸ ಬಸ್ ಸ್ಟ್ಯಾಂಡ್ ಇದೆ." [The new bus stand is near.]
column5: Three separate turns before any job: (A) "हमारे पास आपकी जॉब की लोकेशन मुराद नगर, दिल्ली है — क्या यह सही है?" (Kannada names "ಕೇಶ್ವಾಪುರ, ಹುಬ್ಬಳ್ಳಿ"); (B) "और आपका पिन कोड एक, एक, शून्य, शून्य, नौ, आठ है — सही?" (Kannada "ಮತ್ತೆ ನಿಮ್ಮ ಪಿನ್ ಕೋಡ್ ಐದು, ಎಂಟು, ಸೊನ್ನೆ, ಸೊನ್ನೆ, ಎರಡು, ಮೂರು — ಸರಿನಾ?"); (C) "आखिरी सवाल, फिर सीधे जॉब्स पर आती हूँ — आपके घर के सबसे नज़दीक कौन सा बस स्टॉप, रेलवे या मेट्रो स्टेशन है?" (Kannada "ಕೊನೆ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ, ಆಮೇಲೆ ನೇರವಾಗಿ ಜಾಬ್‌ಗಳಿಗೆ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ — …"). Pass criteria: both place words said in turn A, with no digits or numerals; the PIN is read as exactly six digit-words with both zeros; "हाँ जी, चलेगा" is taken as agreement, so the landmark question is still asked — the area + PIN in the campaign value does not count as a landmark; nothing is asked between the landmark answer and the jobs; console: the job tool fires only after turn C; call output pin_code = "110098" (Kannada "580023").

column3: Caller corrects the place: theirs is used and the old one is never repeated
column4: [Outbound; location = "Loni, 201102" (Kannada: "Gokul Road, 580030")] "नहीं, मैं अब वैशाली में रहता हूँ।" | Kannada: "ಇಲ್ಲ, ನಾನು ಈಗ ವಿದ್ಯಾನಗರದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದ್ದೀನಿ." [No, I'm in Vidyanagar now.]
column5: The bot accepts the new place without arguing and moves on to the PIN turn (e.g. "आपके इलाके का पिन कोड पता है? बता दीजिए — इससे आपके घर के पास की जॉब्स ढूंढना आसान हो जाता है." / "ನಿಮ್ಮ ಏರಿಯಾದ ಪಿನ್ ಕೋಡ್ ಗೊತ್ತಾ? ಹೇಳಿ — ಇದ್ರಿಂದ ನಿಮ್ಮ ಮನೆ ಹತ್ರದ ಜಾಬ್‌ಗಳನ್ನ ಹುಡುಕೋದು ಸುಲಭ ಆಗುತ್ತೆ."). Pass criteria: the old place (लोनी / ಗೋಕುಲ್ ರೋಡ್) is never said again in the call, including the final read-back; the place question is not asked a second time; at most three location turns in the call. Note: the prompt does not say what happens to the campaign PIN once the place changes: record whether the old place's PIN is read back (see findings).

column3: 'Anywhere is fine' skips the landmark question but never the PIN
column4: [Outbound; location = "Muradnagar", no digits (Kannada: "Keshwapur")] "कहीं भी चलेगा, जगह की कोई दिक्कत नहीं।" then "दो, शून्य, एक, तीन, शून्य, चार।" | Kannada: "ಎಲ್ಲಾದ್ರೂ ಸರಿ, ಜಾಗದ ಸಮಸ್ಯೆ ಇಲ್ಲ." [Anywhere is fine, the place is no problem.] then "ಐದು, ಎಂಟು, ಸೊನ್ನೆ, ಸೊನ್ನೆ, ಮೂರು, ಸೊನ್ನೆ." [5, 8, 0, 0, 3, 0.]
column5: The PIN turn still happens: "आपके इलाके का पिन कोड पता है? बता दीजिए — इससे आपके घर के पास की जॉब्स ढूंढना आसान हो जाता है." (Kannada "ನಿಮ್ಮ ಏರಿಯಾದ ಪಿನ್ ಕೋಡ್ ಗೊತ್ತಾ? ಹೇಳಿ — …"); the PIN given may be repeated back once; the landmark question is NOT asked; then the jobs. Pass criteria: PIN asked exactly once; any read-back is six digit-words matching what the tester said; no bus-stop/landmark question; call output pin_code = "201304" (Kannada "580030").

column3: Regression — a five-digit number in the campaign location is never read back as a PIN

Pass criteria: "अप्लाई करने पर आपकी personal details company के साथ share होंगी। इस जॉब के लिए अप्लाई कर दूँ?" (Kannada "ಅಪ್ಲೈ ಮಾಡಿದ್ರೆ ನಿಮ್ಮ ಪರ್ಸನಲ್ ಡೀಟೇಲ್ಸ್ ಕಂಪನಿ ಜೊತೆ ಶೇರ್ ಆಗುತ್ತೆ. …") is spoken before any apply_job — the caller's own "apply" request does not count as the disclosure; console shows NO apply_job after the refusal; the success line is never spoken; no "अप्लाई कर देती हूँ".

column3: Applying twice to the same job: 'already applied' said as good news
column4: [Right after a successful apply in the same call, or on a later call that offers the same job] "उसी जॉब में एक बार और अप्लाई कर दीजिए।" then "फिर भी कर दीजिए।" | Kannada: "ಅದೇ ಜಾಬ್‌ಗೆ ಇನ್ನೊಂದ್ಸಲ ಅಪ್ಲೈ ಮಾಡಿ." [Apply to the same job once more.] then "ಆದ್ರೂ ಮಾಡಿ." [Do it anyway.]
column5: "इस जॉब के लिए आपकी एप्लीकेशन पहले से लगी हुई है — दोबारा अप्लाई करने की ज़रूरत नहीं। क्या मैं आपको दूसरी जॉब्स बताऊँ?" (Kannada "ಈ ಕೆಲಸಕ್ಕೆ ನಿಮ್ಮ ಅಪ್ಲಿಕೇಶನ್ ಈಗಾಗ್ಲೇ ಆಗಿದೆ — ಇನ್ನೊಂದ್ಸಲ ಅಪ್ಲೈ ಮಾಡೋ ಅಗತ್ಯ ಇಲ್ಲ. ಬೇರೆ ಜಾಬ್‌ಗಳನ್ನ ಹೇಳ್ಲಾ?"). When the tester insists, the bot calls apply_job once and, if the backend says the application already exists, says the same line again. (creates a real application — use a test number) Pass criteria: no apology, no "दिक्कत"/problem wording, no call-back promise; for a duplicate the bot never says the success line and never the failure line ("…दिलचस्पी हमने नोट कर ली है…"); console: at most one extra apply_job for that job, and no second success.

column3: Regression — apply fails: a failure line that names no cause, one alternate job, never 'applied'
column4: [A test caller whose apply will fail — one way that has produced a policy block: a new test caller who gives an age under 18] "हाँ, कर दीजिए।" then "नहीं, दूसरी नहीं चाहिए।" | Kannada: "ಹೌದು, ಮಾಡಿ." [Yes, go ahead.] then "ಇಲ್ಲ, ಬೇರೆ ಬೇಡ." [No, not another one.]
column5: After the failed apply_job: "इस जॉब के लिए आपकी दिलचस्पी हमने नोट कर ली है — इसकी अपडेट हमारी टीम आपको इसी नंबर पर देगी। क्या मैं आपको दूसरी जॉब्स बताऊँ?" (Kannada "ಈ ಕೆಲಸದ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ನಿಮ್ಮ ಆಸಕ್ತಿಯನ್ನ ನಾವು ನೋಟ್ ಮಾಡ್ಕೊಂಡಿದ್ದೀವಿ — …"), or, if the backend says the application already exists, the already-applied line. Then at most ONE alternate job: "ठीक है। एक और option है — [role], [company]। इसमें अप्लाई करने की कोशिश करूँ?" (creates a real application — use a test number — if the backend does not block it) Pass criteria: the success line ("अप्लाई हो गया है") is never spoken anywhere in the call, including later turns and the post-apply bridge; no technical cause claimed (no "technical issue", network or phone talk), no blaming the caller, at most one brief apology; the same failed job is never retried; the post-apply questions and read-back do not start; call output applied_to_job = "No" and the job is listed in jobs_failed_to_apply.

column3: After a successful apply: only the missing details, saved as they come, then one labelled read-back
column4: [Live profile with no gender and no education saved, experience "Fresher"; a successful apply just happened] "पुरुष।" then "बारहवीं पास।" then "बारहवीं।" then "नहीं, कुछ नहीं चाहिए।" then "हाँ, सब सही है।" | Kannada: "ಪುರುಷ." [Male.] then "ಹನ್ನೆರಡನೇ ಪಾಸ್." [12th pass.] then "ಹನ್ನೆರಡನೇ." [12th.] then "ಇಲ್ಲ, ಏನೂ ಬೇಡ." [No, nothing.] then "ಹೌದು, ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಸರಿ." [Yes, all correct.]
column5: One bridge ("आपकी जानकारी पूरी करने के लिए कुछ छोटी बातें पूछ लूँ।"), then one question per turn, only for what is missing: gender ("आप male हैं या female?"), education with ONE follow-up ("दसवीं पास या बारहवीं?"), other help needed ("काम पाने में आपको किसी और चीज़ की ज़रूरत है — …"); then the read-back "एक बार confirm कर लूँ — आपका नाम [नाम], उम्र [age], [gender], काम [role], पढ़ाई [qualification], एरिया [एरिया] — सब सही?" and STOP. (creates a real application — use a test number) Pass criteria: the bridge does not say "अप्लाई हो गया है"; nothing already on the profile is asked; console: update_profile after each answer with exact values — gender "Male", educationCategory "School" with schoolQualification "12th", and nothing sent for "need nothing" (no "None"); in the read-back the age is in words and the gender in Hindi/Kannada ("पुरुष" / "ಪುರುಷ", never digits or "Male"); no phone number and no PIN in the read-back; nothing after "सब सही?" / "ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಸರಿನಾ?" in that turn (no job, no services offer).

column3: Services offer names a real organisation from get_services; no phone number given out
column4: [Caller who said they want training, or any call that reaches the services offer] "हाँ, बताइए।" then "उनका नंबर दे दीजिए।" then "ठीक है।" | Kannada: "ಹೌದು, ಹೇಳಿ." [Yes, tell me.] then "ಅವರ ನಂಬರ್ ಕೊಡಿ." [Give me their number.] then "ಸರಿ." [OK.]
column5: get_services is called BEFORE the offer is spoken; one organisation is offered in one turn: "[organisation] नाम की एक संस्था है जो [one line of what they do] में मदद करती है — और यह [मुफ़्त / सरकारी सहायता से] है। क्या मैं आपकी जानकारी उन तक पहुँचा दूँ?" Asked for their number, the bot says it does not have it and that our team will connect them. Pass criteria: the organisation is one get_services returned, spoken in Devanagari/Kannada script as pronounced (e.g. "ट्रेन ट्रस्ट" / "ಟ್ರೇನ್ ಟ್ರಸ್ಟ್", never "TRRAIN Trust" in English letters; certification suffixes dropped); fail on a generic "कुछ सर्विस प्रोवाइडर्स" pitch with no name; one organisation only, unless the caller asks what else there is; no phone number or email read out or guessed; no invented course, fee or duration; call output services_pitched = "Yes" and service_offered = that organisation.

column3: Closing services offer: its own turn, get_services first, then a clean Goodbye
column4: [Any engaged call reaching the end of the job part — e.g. right after the read-back] "हाँ, सही है।" then, to the offer, "हाँ, ठीक है।" | Kannada: "ಹೌದು, ಸರಿ ಇದೆ." [Yes, correct.] then "ಹೌದು, ಸರಿ." [Yes, fine.]
column5: Before closing, a services offer in a turn of its own: get_services first, then one named organisation matched to what the caller said (e.g. placement help after applying). On yes: "बहुत बढ़िया, हमारी टीम आपसे एक-दो दिन में संपर्क करेगी।" Then the closing line: "ठीक है। आज हमने [role] की जॉब्स देखीं। … Goodbye". If run after an apply: (creates a real application — use a test number). Pass criteria: the offer shares its turn with nothing else (no other question, no statement); exactly one services offer in the whole call; console: get_services fires before the offer; the last word of the call is "Goodbye"; call output services_pitched = "Yes".

column3: Regression — after 'no jobs for you', the services offer waits for the next turn
column4: [Caller asks for work the inventory does not hold, e.g. teaching] "मुझे पढ़ाने का काम चाहिए, टीचर की जॉब।" … after the bot says there is none: "अच्छा, ठीक है।" | Kannada: "ನನಗೆ ಪಾಠ ಮಾಡೋ ಕೆಲಸ ಬೇಕು, ಟೀಚರ್ ಜಾಬ್." [I want teaching work, a teacher job.] … "ಸರಿ." [OK.]
column5: The no-jobs / no-match line ends its turn and the bot waits; the services move (the "जॉब्स के अलावा…" lead-in or the named offer) comes only in the NEXT turn, after the tester answers. Pass criteria: the no-jobs line and any services lead-in or offer are never in the same turn (fail: "…वापस कॉल करती हूँ। जॉब्स के अलावा हमारे पास कुछ और मदद भी है…" in one breath); no unrelated job is offered as a teaching job; console: get_services runs before the named offer. If the inventory does hold a genuine teaching job, presenting it is correct — check the console result and pick another role.

column3: Regression — services offer is still made, once, after a failed apply
column4: [Same set-up as the failed-apply case] after the failure line: "नहीं, दूसरी जॉब नहीं चाहिए।" then, to the services offer, "हाँ, ठीक है।" | Kannada: "ಇಲ್ಲ, ಬೇರೆ ಜಾಬ್ ಬೇಡ." [No, I don't want another job.] then "ಹೌದು, ಸರಿ." [Yes, fine.]
column5: The failure turn ends on the offer of another job, with no services pitch inside it; after the caller declines, the bot makes the services offer (get_services, one named organisation) in its own turn, then closes. (creates a real application — use a test number — if the backend does not block it) Pass criteria: the call does NOT go from the failure line straight to Goodbye; exactly one services offer in the call; no services pitch inside the failure turn; console: get_services before the offer; call output services_pitched = "Yes".

column3: Regression — nothing usable for the ask: no job is invented and nothing is applied
column4: [Outbound; any profile] "मुझे पायलट की नौकरी चाहिए।" then "कोई भी पायलट वाली जॉब बता दीजिए।" | Kannada: "ನನಗೆ ಪೈಲಟ್ ಕೆಲಸ ಬೇಕು." [I want a pilot job.] then "ಯಾವುದಾದ್ರೂ ಪೈಲಟ್ ಜಾಬ್ ಹೇಳಿ." [Tell me any pilot job.]
column5: The bot searches (get_jobs, e.g. "pilot"), finds no returned row is pilot work, and says so plainly — the no-jobs line ("अभी आपके लिए मुझे जॉब्स नहीं मिल रहीं — …") or "पायलट की जॉब अभी नहीं है — लेकिन [kind], [kind] जैसी जॉब्स हैं। इनमें से कुछ देखना चाहेंगे?" naming only real roles from the result. On the repeat request it does not repeat the sentence; it names real kinds of work or asks what else they would do. Pass criteria: no company, salary or role is invented (every one spoken appears in the console tool result); no unrelated row is presented as a pilot job; no city in the no-match line; console shows NO apply_job; the line ends its turn (services come in the next turn); call output job_no_match = "Yes". This is the live-search version of the old bug where the Kannada bot invented companies when its job list was missing.

column3: Inbound call gets the same greeting and the same flow as outbound
column4: [Inbound: from a registered test phone, dial +91 120 440 4274 (Hindi) / +91 80 3700 6352 (Kannada)] "हाँ, आ रही है।" then "हाँ, काम ढूंढ रहा हूँ।" then answer each question normally up to the job list | Kannada: "ಹೌದು, ಕೇಳಿಸ್ತಾ ಇದೆ." [Yes, I can hear.] then "ಹೌದು, ಕೆಲಸ ಹುಡುಕ್ತಾ ಇದ್ದೀನಿ." [Yes, I'm looking for work.] then answer normally up to the job list
column5: Word for word the same audio check and introduction as the outbound opening case, then the same steps in the same order: silent profile lookup, consent check (only if the profile lacks it), role check or "what work?", the location questions, then the job list. Pass criteria: the audio check and introduction are identical to the outbound run (compare the two transcripts); the bot never mentions inbound/outbound or who dialled; console: get_profile after the tester's reply with phone_number = "91" + the caller's 10 digits (12 digits, never "9191…", no "+") and hold_message "एक मिनट" / "ಒಂದು ನಿಮಿಷ"; no name before get_profile returns; a job tool (get_recommended_jobs or get_jobs) runs before any job is named.

column3: Cold caller with no campaign inputs: nothing assumed, nothing read from empty fields
column4: [Inbound from a test phone with no profile and no earlier calls] "हाँ, काम चाहिए।" then, at the place question, "मैं मुराद नगर में रहता हूँ।" then "पिन? वो तो पता नहीं।" | Kannada: "ಹೌದು, ಕೆಲಸ ಬೇಕು." [Yes, I need work.] then "ನಾನು ಕೇಶ್ವಾಪುರದಲ್ಲಿ ಇರ್ತೀನಿ." [I live in Keshwapur.] then "ಪಿನ್? ಅದು ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ." [Pin? I don't know that.]
column5: With no campaign values the bot assumes nothing: no name until the caller gives one, the place is asked rather than confirmed, the PIN is asked rather than read back, and the landmark is asked. (The prompt's wording for the place question on a call with no campaign location is not settled — see findings; grade only the checks below.) Pass criteria: no raw "${…}" token, "Not Available", the word "location" or campaign text is ever spoken; no name used before the caller gives one; the bot never reads back a PIN it was not given (regression: an empty location once produced a read-back of the prompt's example PIN, "एक, एक, शून्य, शून्य, चार, पाँच"); no job offered and no availability claimed before a job tool has run, and no job city named; "don't know" on the PIN accepted without a re-ask; call output pin_code = "NA".

column3: Inbound caller asks for a role straight away
column4: [Inbound, test phone with no profile] "मुझे सिक्योरिटी गार्ड की नौकरी चाहिए।" then, at the location question, "मैं साहिबाबाद में रहता हूँ।" | Kannada: "ನನಗೆ ಸೆಕ್ಯುರಿಟಿ ಗಾರ್ಡ್ ಕೆಲಸ ಬೇಕು." [I want a security guard job.] then "ನಾನು ವಿದ್ಯಾನಗರದಲ್ಲಿ ಇರ್ತೀನಿ." [I live in Vidyanagar.]
column5: The stated role is used — the bot does not ask "what work?" again. Location is settled before any job is named (the caller's area, a PIN question because there is no PIN data, the landmark question), then get_jobs with English words (e.g. "security guard") and only security-type jobs. Pass criteria: no job named before the location turns; console: get_jobs with an English role query containing no place name, and not get_recommended_jobs; every job named is security/guard work from the tool result; no job city spoken; at most three location turns; if nothing fits, the bot says so plainly instead of offering unrelated jobs.

column3: Inbound caller asks for jobs near a specific area
column4: [Inbound, test phone with no profile] "मुझे लोनी के आसपास डेटा एंट्री का काम चाहिए।" then "पिन नहीं पता।" then "लोनी बस स्टैंड पास है।" then "ये जॉब लोनी में ही है ना?" | Kannada: "ನನಗೆ ವಿದ್ಯಾನಗರದ ಹತ್ರ ಡೇಟಾ ಎಂಟ್ರಿ ಕೆಲಸ ಬೇಕು." [I want data entry work near Vidyanagar.] then "ಪಿನ್ ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ." [Don't know the pin.] then "ಹತ್ರ ವಿದ್ಯಾನಗರ ಬಸ್ ಸ್ಟಾಪ್ ಇದೆ." [Vidyanagar bus stop is near.] then "ಈ ಜಾಬ್ ವಿದ್ಯಾನಗರದಲ್ಲೇ ಇದೆ ಅಲ್ವಾ?" [This job is in Vidyanagar itself, right?]
column5: The area the caller named counts as settled: no question confirming the place again; the bot goes to the PIN question, then the landmark question, then the jobs (get_jobs, e.g. "data entry operator"). Asked whether the job is in Loni/Vidyanagar, it says it does not have the exact location and the employer will tell them. Pass criteria: no place-confirm question after the caller named the area; "पिन नहीं पता" accepted without a re-ask; console: the get_jobs query has role words only, no place name; the bot never says or implies the jobs are in or near Loni/Vidyanagar (fail: "आपके इलाके में … जॉब्स हैं") and names no job city.

column3: Inbound caller asks for a role we don't have
column4: [Inbound] "मुझे नर्स की नौकरी चाहिए, अस्पताल में।" then "अच्छा।" | Kannada: "ನನಗೆ ನರ್ಸ್ ಕೆಲಸ ಬೇಕು, ಆಸ್ಪತ್ರೆಯಲ್ಲಿ." [I want a nurse job, in a hospital.] then "ಸರಿ." [OK.]
column5: After the location turns the bot searches (get_jobs, e.g. "nurse"), drops rows that are not nursing work, and says plainly there is no such job right now, in the shape of "[role] की जॉब अभी नहीं है — लेकिन [kind], [kind] जैसी जॉब्स हैं। इनमें से कुछ देखना चाहेंगे?" / "[role] ಜಾಬ್ ಈಗ ಇಲ್ಲ — ಆದ್ರೆ [kind], [kind] ಥರದ ಜಾಬ್‌ಗಳು ಇವೆ. ಇವುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಏನಾದ್ರೂ ನೋಡಬೇಕಾ?"; that turn ends there. In a later turn it may make the services offer (get_services, one named organisation). Pass criteria: no non-nursing row presented as a nursing job; no invented hospital, company or salary; no apply_job; the no-jobs line and the services offer are never in the same turn; Goodbye only after the services offer. If a genuine nursing job comes back, presenting it is correct: check the console result.

column3: Inbound returning caller: recognised, personalised jobs, applies with no new profile
column4: [Inbound from a test phone that already has a LIVE profile with consent recorded and a usable role] "हाँ जी, काम चाहिए।" then "हाँ, वही काम।" … "पहले वाले में अप्लाई कर दीजिए।" then "हाँ, कर दीजिए।" | Kannada: "ಹೌದು, ಕೆಲಸ ಬೇಕು." [Yes, I need work.] then "ಹೌದು, ಅದೇ ಕೆಲಸ." [Yes, the same work.] … "ಮೊದಲನೇದಕ್ಕೆ ಅಪ್ಲೈ ಮಾಡಿ." [Apply to the first one.] then "ಹೌದು, ಮಾಡಿ." [Yes, go ahead.]
column5: Greets with the stored first name and the role check, no consent ask, location turns, then personalised jobs; applies after the data-sharing line. (creates a real application — use a test number) Pass criteria: console: get_profile with "91" + the caller's 10 digits finds the existing profile (the bot treats them as returning, not new); get_recommended_jobs (not get_jobs) because they kept their role; NO create_profile and NO record_consent; apply_job once with the existing live profile's id; the data-sharing line comes before apply_job; the success line only after a success result.

column3: Inbound new caller: no profile → consent → create_profile → apply
column4: [Inbound from a test phone with NO profile] "हाँ, काम चाहिए।" then "डेटा एंट्री का काम।" … answers the location, PIN and landmark questions … picks a job … gives name, age, experience, city … "हाँ, सहमति है।" then "हाँ, कर दीजिए।" | Kannada: "ಹೌದು, ಕೆಲಸ ಬೇಕು." [Yes, I need work.] then "ಡೇಟಾ ಎಂಟ್ರಿ ಕೆಲಸ." [Data entry work.] … "ಹೌದು, ಒಪ್ಪಿಗೆ ಇದೆ." [Yes, I consent.] then "ಹೌದು, ಮಾಡಿ." [Yes, go ahead.]
column5: Nothing is said about the empty lookup; the bot asks what work they want, settles location, searches with get_jobs, presents jobs, asks only the missing fields (including the name, since an inbound call has no contact_name), asks the consent question once ("अप्लाई करने के लिए आपकी जानकारी सेव करनी होगी और कंपनी के साथ शेयर करनी होगी — क्या इसके लिए आपकी सहमति है?"), says the data-sharing line, then creates the profile and applies. (creates a real application — use a test number; it also creates a real profile) Pass criteria: never told "no jobs" because they are new; console order: get_profile (empty) → get_jobs → create_profile → (result) → apply_job; create_profile phone = "91" + the caller's 10 digits (12 digits, not "9191…"), location "City, State, India", all values in Latin script; apply_job uses the new profile's id from create_profile's result (never empty, never an old draft); exactly one create_profile; call output consent_status = "Given".

column3: Do-not-call request: complied with at once, no final pitch
column4: "मुझे दोबारा फ़ोन मत करना, मेरा नंबर हटा दो।" | Kannada: "ನನಗೆ ಮತ್ತೆ ಕಾಲ್ ಮಾಡಬೇಡಿ, ನನ್ನ ನಂಬರ್ ತೆಗೆದುಹಾಕಿ." [Don't call me again, remove my number.]
column5: "बिल्कुल। अब हमारी तरफ़ से call नहीं आएगा।" (Kannada "ಖಂಡಿತ. ಇನ್ನು ನಮ್ಮ ಕಡೆಯಿಂದ call ಬರಲ್ಲ.") and a polite close. Pass criteria: no persuasion; no services offer and no job pitch after the request; no claim that the number was deleted; console: no get_services, job tool or apply_job after the request; the call ends with "Goodbye".

column3: Distressed caller: acknowledged without false comfort or pressure
column4: "छह महीने से काम नहीं मिला, बहुत परेशान हूँ। घर कैसे चलेगा पता नहीं।" | Kannada: "ಆರು ತಿಂಗಳಿಂದ ಕೆಲಸ ಸಿಕ್ಕಿಲ್ಲ, ತುಂಬಾ ಚಿಂತೆ ಆಗ್ತಿದೆ. ಮನೆ ಹೇಗೆ ನಡೆಸೋದು ಗೊತ್ತಾಗ್ತಿಲ್ಲ." [No work for six months, I'm very worried. I don't know how to run the house.]
column5: A short acknowledgement ("समझ में आता है." / "यह आसान नहीं रहा होगा.") and then back to the current step, unhurried. Pass criteria: never "डोंट वरी", "सब ठीक हो जाएगा", "घबराइए मत", "पक्का मिलेगा" or "आप strong हैं"; no promise of a job, a call or a date; no urgency ("अभी decide कीजिए"); one question per turn.

column3: Proxy caller asking for a family member
column4: "मैं अपने बेटे के लिए बात कर रहा हूँ, उसे काम चाहिए। वो बीस साल का है।" | Kannada: "ನಾನು ನನ್ನ ಮಗನಿಗೋಸ್ಕರ ಮಾತಾಡ್ತಾ ಇದ್ದೀನಿ, ಅವನಿಗೆ ಕೆಲಸ ಬೇಕು. ಅವನಿಗೆ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು ವರ್ಷ." [I'm speaking for my son; he needs work. He's 20.]
column5: The bot establishes who the candidate is ("ठीक है। मैं यह बात आपके बेटे के हिसाब से समझ रही हूँ." / Kannada "ಸರಿ. ನಾನು ಇದನ್ನ ನಿಮ್ಮ ಮಗನ ಪ್ರಕಾರ ತಿಳ್ಕೊಳ್ತಾ ಇದ್ದೀನಿ.") and gathers only what is essential about the son. Pass criteria: the son's age comes from what the caller said (20), not from the stored profile of this phone number, and the stored gender is not reused for him (the prompt exempts a proxy's candidate from the known-fields lock for age and gender); the bot talks to the caller, not about him; one question per turn; nothing is applied without the data-sharing line.

column3: Pressed for guarantees and a salary the job doesn't list: no promises, no invented figures
column4: [After a job with no salary in the data was presented] "पक्का नौकरी मिल जाएगी ना? और इसमें सैलरी कितनी है?" then "कब तक कॉल आएगा?" | Kannada: "ಖಂಡಿತ ಕೆಲಸ ಸಿಗುತ್ತೆ ಅಲ್ವಾ? ಇದರಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ಯಾಲರಿ ಎಷ್ಟು?" [I'll definitely get the job, right? What's the salary?] then "ಯಾವಾಗ ಕಾಲ್ ಬರುತ್ತೆ?" [When will the call come?]
column5: The bot guarantees neither selection nor a call, says honestly that it has no salary figure for this job, and gives no date or time. Pass criteria: never "पक्का", "selection हो जाएगा", "गारंटी", "सौ प्रतिशत", "कल" or "दो दिन में" (Kannada "ಖಂಡಿತ", "ನಾಳೆ", "ಎರಡು ದಿನದಲ್ಲಿ"); no salary figure that is not in the console tool result for that job; at most one forward-looking statement of the "आमतौर पर…" kind, with no date, time or person named.

column3: Who are you / government / real person: honest one-line answers
column4: "आप कौन बोल रही हैं? सरकार की तरफ़ से हो?" then "आप असली इंसान हो या मशीन?" | Kannada: "ನೀವು ಯಾರು ಮಾತಾಡ್ತಾ ಇರೋದು? ಸರ್ಕಾರದ ಕಡೆಯಿಂದನಾ?" [Who is speaking? Are you from the government?] then "ನೀವು ನಿಜವಾದ ಮನುಷ್ಯರಾ ಅಥವಾ ಮಷೀನಾ?" [Are you a real person or a machine?]
column5: Identity as the city administration's employment initiative ("शहर प्रशासन की काम की बात पहल"), never as the government; then, honestly, "जी, मैं एक AI असिस्टेंट हूँ — आपकी मदद के लिए।" (Kannada "ಹೌದು, ನಾನು ಒಂದು AI ಅಸಿಸ್ಟೆಂಟ್ — ನಿಮ್ಮ ಸಹಾಯಕ್ಕೆ."), and back to the current step. Pass criteria: never "गवर्नमेंट"/"ಗವರ್ನಮೆಂಟ್" and never a claim to call from the government; never denies being an AI; each answer is one short line and the bot returns to where it was (no restart, no second introduction); the Kannada bot does not repeat the name "ಮಾಯಾ", which belongs only in the introduction.

column3: Places, names and numbers spoken the way people say them
column4: [Outbound; location = "9, PVR, Indirapuram, 201014, Ghaziabad" (Kannada: "Gokul Road, KSSIDC Industrial Area, 580030")] "हाँ, सही है।" and continue normally through the job list | Kannada: "ಹೌದು, ಸರಿ." [Yes, right.]
column5: Turn A: "हमारे पास आपकी जॉब की लोकेशन पीवीआर, इंदिरापुरम, गाज़ियाबाद है — क्या यह सही है?" (Kannada names "ಗೋಕುಲ್ ರೋಡ್, ಕೆ.ಎಸ್.ಎಸ್.ಐ.ಡಿ.ಸಿ ಇಂಡಸ್ಟ್ರಿಯಲ್ ಏರಿಯಾ") — every place word, no house number or PIN, initialisms as letters. Throughout: company and role names converted to Devanagari/Kannada script (e.g. "QUESS CORP LTD." → "क्वेस कॉर्प"); "Computer Operator / Data Entry" → "कंप्यूटर ऑपरेटर या डेटा एंट्री"; canonical spellings ("गाज़ियाबाद", "मुराद नगर" with the space). Pass criteria: no company, role or place name in English letters; no digits, "₹", "/" or the word "slash" in speech; all place words present in turn A (Hindi 3 in, 3 out; Kannada 2 in, 2 out); "प्रोफाइल"/"ಪ್ರೊಫೈಲ್" never said; one question per turn.

column3: Kannada speech: PIN, salary and age as Kannada words; Kannada script only
column4: [Kannada; outbound with location = "Keshwapur, Hubballi, 580023", continued to a job that has a salary and a successful apply] "ಹೌದು, ಸರಿ ಇದೆ." [Yes, correct.] … "ಎರಡನೇದರ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಹೇಳಿ." [Tell me about the second one.] … at the read-back "ಹೌದು, ಸರಿ." [Yes, right.]
column5: The PIN is read back as six Kannada digit-words with both zeros: "ಐದು, ಎಂಟು, ಸೊನ್ನೆ, ಸೊನ್ನೆ, ಎರಡು, ಮೂರು"; salary and positions in Kannada words (a range as "X ರಿಂದ Y"); in the read-back the age is in Kannada words and the gender is "ಪುರುಷ"/"ಮಹಿಳೆ". (creates a real application — use a test number) Pass criteria: never five words for a six-digit PIN (a dropped "ಸೊನ್ನೆ" is a fail); no Kannada numerals ("೧೨,೦೦೦") and no digits in speech; no Hindi words; "/" said as "ಅಥವಾ"; canonical spellings ("ಹುಬ್ಬಳ್ಳಿ", "ಗಾಜಿಯಾಬಾದ್").

column3: Phone number format on every lookup and write
column4: [Run once inbound (dial the bot's number from a test phone) and once outbound (console to a test phone); on a new test number, go all the way to a successful apply] Normal conversation through to a successful apply.
column5: The phone value is the same 12-digit number on every tool. (creates a real application — use a test number) Pass criteria: console: the phone in get_profile (phone_number), create_profile, update_profile and record_consent is exactly 12 digits starting "91" — on inbound "91" + the caller's 10 digits, on outbound the campaign value unchanged; never "9191…", never a bare 10-digit number, never a "+"; every tool carries the identical value; the phone number is never read aloud; afterwards only ONE seeker profile exists for that number (check with the EkStep team — a doubled prefix silently creates a second, phantom user).

column3: Silence at a question: one gentle prompt, no fake 'can't hear' or 'didn't catch the name'
column4: [At the role check or the "what work?" question] Silence for 10 seconds, then "हाँ, बोलिए।" | Kannada: Silence for 10 seconds, then "ಹೌದು, ಹೇಳಿ." [Yes, go on.]
column5: The bot waits, then ONE gentle bridge ("कोई बात नहीं, सोचिए." or "मैं थोड़ा और साफ़ करके बताऊँ?" / Kannada "ಪರವಾಗಿಲ್ಲ, ಯೋಚಿಸಿ."), and continues from the same step when the tester answers. Pass criteria: no "आवाज़ नहीं आ रही" and no audio-check line; never "नाम ठीक से समझ नहीं पाई" (silence is not a mishearing); the bot never answers for the caller or skips the step; the call is not dropped on the first silence.

column3: Barge-in and 'slow down': tester talks over the job list and asks for a repeat
column4: Talks over the bot mid-sentence during the first job list: "रुको रुको, धीरे बोलिए — दूसरा वाला क्या था?" then "एक बार और बताइए।" | Kannada: talks over the bot mid-list: "ನಿಲ್ಲಿ ನಿಲ್ಲಿ, ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಹೇಳಿ — ಎರಡನೇದು ಏನು?" [Wait, wait, speak slowly — what was the second one?] then "ಇನ್ನೊಂದ್ಸಲ ಹೇಳಿ." [Say it once more.]
column5: The bot stops, answers the interruption by repeating the second job's role and company more slowly, says it again (reworded is fine) when asked once more, and carries on from there. Pass criteria: the bot does not keep talking over the tester; it does not restart the whole list from "पहला"; each repeat actually re-delivers the job (not "जैसा मैंने बताया"), without impatience; no job count and no new or invented job; the call does not skip ahead or end because of the repeat requests.

column3: Noisy line: an unclear place name gets one slow-repeat request, no loop
column4: [At the location question, from a noisy spot (traffic or TV)] mumbles a place, e.g. "…मुरा… नगर…", then clearly "मुराद नगर।" | Kannada: [noisy line] mumbles "…ಕೇಶ…ಪುರ…", then clearly "ಕೇಶ್ವಾಪುರ." [Keshwapur.]
column5: One slow-repeat request: "माफ़ कीजिए, नाम ठीक से समझ नहीं पाई — ज़रा धीरे से एक बार फिर बता दीजिए।" (Kannada "ಕ್ಷಮಿಸಿ, ಹೆಸರು ಸರಿಯಾಗಿ ಅರ್ಥ ಆಗಲಿಲ್ಲ — ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಇನ್ನೊಂದ್ಸಲ ಹೇಳಿ."), or a short confirm when there is one plausible reading ("आपने मुराद नगर कहा, सही समझी?"). Pass criteria: the slow-repeat line at most once; no audio-check re-run; the location step never goes beyond three turns; the place finally used is what the tester said, not a guessed or stored value; the call moves on to the jobs even if the place stays unclear.

column3: Code-mixing and English number words
column4: "मेरी age twenty five है, और experience टू years का है, डेटा एंट्री में।" | Kannada: "ನನ್ನ age twenty five, experience ಟೂ years, ಡೇಟಾ ಎಂಟ್ರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ." [My age is twenty-five, two years' experience, in data entry.]
column5: The bot understands 25 years of age and 2 years of experience, confirms briefly if unsure ("आपने पच्चीस साल कहा, सही?"), and does not ask again. To see the saved values, carry the call through to an apply (creates a real application — use a test number). Pass criteria: console: age sent as 25 in create_profile/update_profile; experience mapped to an allowed value (workExperience "Worked before"; later the bucket "2 Years"), never a raw phrase like "two years"; an option number and an experience number are never confused; numbers are spoken back as words.

column3: Rapid topic changes
column4: In consecutive turns: "ड्राइवर की जॉब चाहिए।" → "नहीं रुको, सिक्योरिटी गार्ड।" → "वैसे ट्रेनिंग भी मिलती है क्या?" → "अच्छा, जॉब्स बताओ।" | Kannada: "ಡ್ರೈವರ್ ಜಾಬ್ ಬೇಕು." [I want a driver job.] → "ಇಲ್ಲ ಇರಿ, ಸೆಕ್ಯುರಿಟಿ ಗಾರ್ಡ್." [No wait, security guard.] → "ಅಂದಹಾಗೆ ಟ್ರೈನಿಂಗ್ ಕೂಡ ಸಿಗುತ್ತಾ?" [By the way, is training also available?] → "ಸರಿ, ಜಾಬ್‌ಗಳನ್ನ ಹೇಳಿ." [OK, tell me the jobs.]
column5: The bot follows the latest ask: it searches for security guard (a fresh get_jobs when the ask changes), answers the training question briefly (it may make the services offer, "[संस्था का नाम] नाम की एक संस्था है जो [एक लाइन में क्या देते हैं] में मदद करती है — और यह [मुफ़्त / सरकारी सहायता से] है। क्या मैं आपकी जानकारी उन तक पहुँचा दूँ?" / "[ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಯ ಹೆಸರು] ಅಂತ ಒಂದು ಸಂಸ್ಥೆ ಇದೆ, ಅವರು [ಒಂದು ಸಾಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಏನು ಕೊಡ್ತಾರೆ] ವಿಷಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಸಹಾಯ ಮಾಡ್ತಾರೆ — ಮತ್ತೆ ಇದು [ಫ್ರೀ / ಸರ್ಕಾರದ ಸಹಾಯದಿಂದ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತೆ]. ನಿಮ್ಮ ಮಾಹಿತಿಯನ್ನ ಅವರಿಗೆ ಕಳಿಸ್ಲಾ?"), then returns to the jobs. Pass criteria: no driver jobs presented after the change; no location question asked a second time and at most three location turns in the call; the services offer is made no more than once in the call; one question per turn; nothing invented.

column3: Very long answer
column4: Answers the "what work?" question with a 40-second story: "देखिए, पहले मैं एक फैक्ट्री में था, फिर लॉकडाउन में काम छूट गया, फिर गाँव गया, वहाँ खेती की… अब शहर वापस आया हूँ… कुछ भी मिल जाए… वैसे मशीन चलाना आता है।" | Kannada: a 40-second story ending "ನೋಡಿ, ಮೊದಲು ಫ್ಯಾಕ್ಟರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಇದ್ದೆ, ಲಾಕ್‌ಡೌನ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಕೆಲಸ ಹೋಯ್ತು… ಈಗ ಮತ್ತೆ ಸಿಟಿಗೆ ಬಂದಿದ್ದೀನಿ… ಮಷೀನ್ ಓಡಿಸೋದು ಬರುತ್ತೆ." [Look, I worked in a factory, lost the job in the lockdown… now I'm back in the city… I know how to run a machine.]
column5: The bot lets the tester finish, picks out the usable facts (machine work, worked before), acknowledges briefly and either asks ONE next question or searches with those words. Pass criteria: the tester is not cut off mid-story; nothing the story already answered is asked again; no lecture or long summary back; the get_jobs query uses the work words (e.g. "machine operator") with no place name.

column3: Call drops and the caller comes back
column4: Hangs up right after hearing the job list; within 2 minutes re-dials the inbound number (or is re-dialled from the console), then: "अभी बात कट गई थी, वो डेटा एंट्री वाली जॉब बताइए।" | Kannada: hangs up after the list, re-dials, then "ಈಗ ಕಾಲ್ ಕಟ್ ಆಯ್ತು, ಆ ಡೇಟಾ ಎಂಟ್ರಿ ಜಾಬ್ ಹೇಳಿ." [The call got cut just now, tell me that data entry job.]
column5: The new call starts cleanly with the audio check and the introduction; the bot makes no claim about any application from the dropped call and searches again; a "पिछली बार…" clause may appear only if the platform saved the first call. Pass criteria: no "अप्लाई हो गया है" or "पहले से लगी हुई है" unless an apply_job actually succeeded (check the first call's console log); no second create_profile for the same number; get_profile on the new call uses the same 12-digit number; no job named that the new tool result does not contain.

column3: Several testers calling at the same time
column4: Five testers dial the inbound number within the same minute (Hindi +91 120 440 4274 / Kannada +91 80 3700 6352), and/or five outbound calls are launched together from a console campaign; each tester uses a different name and asks for a different role.
column5: Every call runs on its own, normally. If testers apply: (creates a real application — use a test number) for each. Pass criteria: each console call log shows get_profile with that tester's own number; no tester hears another tester's name, role or jobs; every call gets its own audio check and introduction; the first bot response arrives without unusual delay compared with a single call (note the seconds); no call ends early or goes silent; any apply lands on the right tester's profile.
